subject: MAP: milestone-linked burst/overage mechanics and evaluation credit
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@acmessoft.com>; Raj Patel <raj.patel@acmessoft.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff — evaluation period, usage bands, and surge mechanics

Hannah / Raj —

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our MAP kickoff, attached is a short proposal that ties the commercial milestones to the evaluation ramp so both teams have clear expectations on pricing exposure during the proof-of-concept. High level: 

- Milestone 1 (staging): up to 200k tokens/day for 30 days; 
- Milestone 2 (pilot): 1.0M tokens/day for 60 days with controlled burst allowance; 
- Milestone 3 (prod cutover): committed baseline and reserved capacity pricing.

Key open items we flagged that I want to document here so we can close them in the next 48 hours: 
1) How are overages billed during the evaluation window — per-token, per-request, or a blended unit?
2) What is the definition of a "burst" vs sustained overage for invoicing and credits?
3) Can Redwood provide a one-time evaluation overage credit if AcmeSoft signs PO by Sep 10?
4) Any hard usage caps we need to enforce to protect shared pools during staging?

I've attached a one-page MAP (Proposed_MAP_v1.pdf) and a short excerpt from our public rate card (redwood-ratecard-2026Q3.pdf). Please review and confirm which items you'd like tightened or expanded.

Next steps: Hannah, if you agree, can we set a three-way call Monday to lock these items? Ben — happy for you to join to confirm pricing mechanics and margin impact.

Thanks,
Olga
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Proposed_MAP_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@acmessoft.com>

Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — evaluation period, usage bands, and surge mechanics

Olga —

Thanks, got the docs. A few clarifying questions before the call: 

- Unit for overage billing: we need confirmation whether overage is charged per-token (as in your rate card) or per-request. Our internal usage estimator works in "requests" which vary a lot in token consumption. If overage is per-token, can you provide a short sample invoice calculation so our finance team can model?

- Burst behavior: during our load testing we expect several short peaks (30s–3min). Do you treat those short peaks the same as a sustained daily overage? Is there a separate burst multiplier? Also, is there any automated throttling we should anticipate once we exceed the soft cap?

- Evaluation credit ask: AcmeSoft can sign the PO by Sep 10 if Redwood provides a one-time 50% credit on overages for the first 30 days after pilot start. Is that something you can approve at this level or do you need leadership sign-off?

Looping Raj for technical bandwidth — he might have follow-ups on throttling behavior.

Best,
Hannah
Director, AI Products
AcmeSoft

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>; Hannah Lee <hannah.lee@acmessoft.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — evaluation period, usage bands, and surge mechanics

Hannah —

Quick answers below; happy to sync on the call Monday but want these on thread so finance/legal have a record.

1) Overage unit: billed per-token. We bill by input+output tokens in the invoice window. If you want per-request visibility we can provide request-level token logs as part of the MAP (no extra cost). Sample calc: 
   - Rate card publishes $0.0006 / 1k tokens for baseline model; overage applies at the same unit with a multiplier when burst conditions are met. Example invoice line: "Tokens billed: 3,250,000 (3,250 * 1k) x $0.0006 = $1.95" (numbers illustrative).

2) Burst definition & multiplier: we separate short spikes from sustained overruns: 
   - Short bursts: any 5-minute window where usage exceeds soft cap by up to 3x; billed at 1.5x list for the tokens in that window (capped at 72 hours of aggregated bursts per billing cycle).
   - Sustained overage: if average daily usage exceeds the agreed baseline for more than 30 consecutive days, we treat that as a contract-level overage and suggest moving to a committed tier (different pricing).
   - Throttling: we avoid hard throttle during MAP staging unless cluster health is at risk; instead we send warn-alerts and apply burst multiplier to tokens. If a customer requests hard caps we can enforce them via per-route policies.

3) One-time evaluation credit: we can approve a one-time 50% credit on billed overages for the first 30 days of pilot start conditional on: (a) PO signed by 2026-09-10, (b) MAP milestones agreed and tracked, and (c) usage logs shared daily for the 30-day credit window. This has been approved by me for standard deals under $200k ARR; for larger commitments I'll need AC sign-off.

Attachment: redwood-ratecard-2026Q3.pdf (excerpted).

Ben
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-ratecard-2026Q3.pdf (application/pdf)]

Forwarding the thread and Ben's confirmation. Lauren, can you confirm the following from an ops and margin perspective before we lock in the MAP:

- The cap on aggregated burst billing (72 hours / billing cycle) — any ops risks we need to surface to Acme regarding shared cluster exposure?
- Language for the MAP: we need minimal legal text that references the one-time 50% credit and the dependency on daily log sharing. Legal will draft a short clause; ops needs to confirm observability hooks.

I'm attaching the MAP tracker that has milestone dates filled in tentatively (MAP_tracker.xlsx). Hannah, if these points read fine, please confirm PO cadence so Ben can issue an updated commercial term sheet.

Thanks,
Olga
